examples.description: Invoice with its line items in one call (the composite door — preferred)
Draft an invoice header only (attach items later)
Singapore GST tax invoice in US dollars: one standard-rated and one zero-rated (exported) line, with the Singapore-dollar rate IRAS requires on a foreign-currency tax invoice
A cash sale recorded as the amount taken, as the Quick Sale keypad records it: the total and the payment are exactly 45.00, and any tax the business charges is worked out inside it

failure_modes.recovery: Fix the named field and retry — the error lists the writable properties.
failure_modes.when: a field is missing/over-length, status is outside draft/sent/paid/cancelled, or an unknown property was sent

failure_modes.recovery: Call invoice_client_list (or invoice_client_upsert) first, then retry with its id.
failure_modes.when: client_id does not name an invoice_client in your tenant

failure_modes.recovery: Resend with the value the error names: it lists the codes that apply on the issue date and the rate with its source. Under a scheme, leave tax_rate_bps out.
failure_modes.when: tax_scheme is not sg_gst, my_sst or none; a tax_code is not a code of the scheme or does not apply on the issue date; a my_sst line has no tax_code; tax_rate_bps differs from the scheme's rate on the issue date; tax_code, an fx rate or (except on a cash sale invoice) prices_include_tax came without a tax_scheme; or the fx rate is not a positive decimal of up to 6 decimals, comes without fx_rate_date, or is on an SGD or my_sst document

failure_modes.recovery: Send the call without tax_scheme, prices_include_tax, tax_code and the fx fields for now (a cash sale that holds its tax waits: without the flag the rate is added on top); the owner runs `pnpm db:seed` to enable them.
failure_modes.when: a tax scheme field was sent and the platform catalog does not list the tax scheme fields yet (SIMPLER_SALES_TAX_MODEL_UNSEEDED)

preconditions: invoice_number is server-claimed (atomic per-tenant sequence) — any value you send is ignored.

ONE CALL does the whole document: pass `items` [{description, quantity, unit_price_cents}] and the door creates the invoice + all line rows (money in integer CENTS: $15.00 → 1500). Granular invoice_item_create remains for adding lines later.

status 'paid' at creation requires `items` in the SAME call — the door synthesizes the payment fact row for the invoice's total_cents. Header-only birth-'paid' is refused: create, add items, then invoice_payment_record.

share:true returns share_url and the document in the same call (the invoice_share payload). The link is get-or-create and nothing is sent. Pass it only when the user asks for a link: the result already carries the invoice as copy-ready text in its second content block, when it has one.

due_date is epoch millis, and the invoice is due on the calendar day that instant falls on in the business time zone (sales_settings.timezone, unset = Asia/Singapore). For a due date, send 12:00 UTC of that date (30 Sep 2026 = 1790769600000): it falls on that date in every listed zone, while 00:00 UTC falls on the day before west of UTC.

tax_scheme sg_gst (Singapore GST) or my_sst (Malaysia SST) prices each line by its tax_code from Simpler's dated rulebook: sg_gst codes standard (the GST rate on the issue date, 9% since 1 Jan 2024), zero_rated, exempt, out_of_scope; my_sst codes sales_10, sales_5, service_8, service_6, exempt (every my_sst line needs one). Left out, tax_scheme is your sales settings' tax_scheme; "none" (or null) prices by tax_rate_bps as before. Under a scheme, tax_rate_bps is resolved for you: a different value is refused naming the rate and its source. prices_include_tax true means unit prices already include the tax. tax_scheme and prices_include_tax cannot change after creation: create a new document with the ones you want (Duplicate on the web page).

With items, the answer echoes items_total_cents (the lines as sent, added up: check it against your items), subtotal_cents (before tax; under prices that include tax, the net inside them), tax_cents and total_cents (what the document charges; a cash sale's is the amount taken).

description: ONE call creates the whole document: claims the next invoice number, then writes the header plus every line in `items` ([{description, quantity, unit_price_cents}], integer CENTS). client_name finds a client by name or creates one. Birth status 'paid' needs items in the same call. tax_scheme sg_gst or my_sst taxes each line by its tax_code (refusals: see tax_scheme). When present, the second content block is the invoice as copy-ready text, shown with a Copy button where the host draws MCP Apps; if the user says they cannot see the invoice, give them that block word for word; share:true adds a client link, only when the user asks for one. NEXT: invoice_payment_record to record money-in.

client_name.description: Client by NAME — resolves to an existing client or creates one (no client_id lookup needed).

force.description: Confirms a create whose notes or single line item read like a payment RECEIVED or a write-off rather than a new bill — resend the SAME call with force:true to create it anyway. No effect on quote_create (the intent trap is invoice-only).

fx_rate_date.description: The date the fx rate is for, YYYY-MM-DD. Send with fx_rate_to_sgd.

fx_rate_to_sgd.description: sg_gst invoices in a currency other than SGD: Singapore dollars per 1 unit of the invoice currency as a decimal string, up to 6 decimals ("1.3502"), from a source IRAS accepts (MAS, a local bank, Bloomberg, Reuters, Oanda) for the date of supply. Send with fx_rate_date. Or send fx_rate_to_sgd_ppm (1.3502 → 1350200).

items.description: ONE call creates the whole document — line items in integer CENTS ($15.00 → 1500), or unit_price as a decimal string. quantity takes up to 3 decimals (1.5 hours → 1.5); unit is an optional label (hr, kg); discount_bps is an optional line discount (10% → 1000). tax_code is the line's tax under the document's tax_scheme (sg_gst: standard, zero_rated, exempt, out_of_scope, default standard; my_sst: sales_10, sales_5, service_8, service_6, exempt, required); refused without a tax_scheme.

prices_include_tax.description: true = unit prices already include the tax (the tax is worked back out of each line). Default false. Needs a tax_scheme, except on a cash sale (cash_sale 1): its total is then the amount taken, with tax_rate_bps (or your default rate) worked out inside it, as the Quick Sale keypad records it.

share.description: Only when the user asks for a link: true also returns share_url (the client's link to view the invoice) and the full document in this same call. Where this environment has no public address, share_path and share_url_unavailable come back instead of share_url. Nothing is sent.

tax_scheme.description: sg_gst (Singapore GST) or my_sst (Malaysia SST): each line is taxed by its tax_code at the rate in force on the issue date. Under a scheme, a tax_rate_bps other than that rate, an unknown tax_code and a my_sst line without one are refused, naming the valid codes and the rate's source. "none" = no scheme, priced by tax_rate_bps. Left out = your sales settings' tax_scheme.
